1. This petition is filed for seeking quashing of the Fir No.182/2015 under Sections 498A/406/34 of
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Ipc) registered at Police Station Mandawali, Delhi, on the ground of
settlement.

2. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioners no.2 and 3 are
family members of the petitioner no.1.
The marriage of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 7th March, 2011, according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
One minor child was born out of the wedlock.
3. Disputes arose between the parties and their respective families,

sentences.text: Subsequently, the parties have settled their disputes and the terms of the settlement are recorded in the divorce petition filed by the parties under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 annexed as Annexure P-2 (colly) to the petition.
The parties have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide decree dated 25th May, 2016.
5. Issue notice.

6. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and by the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 2.
7.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel and by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
8. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.

9. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
10. There is one minor child born from the wedlock, who is in the care and custody of the respondent no.2/mother.
It is directed that the settlement executed between the petitioners and the respondent no.2 as well as this This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:02:59 order shall have no effect on the rights of the minor child/children in the future.
11. Consequently, FIR No. 182/2015 registered at Police Station Mandawali, Delhi and proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
12. The petition stands disposed of.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023 rt
